yd:
Someone on X built an entire interactive 3D tool of the human anatomy, with accurate models, in a single afternoon.

That is the part worth sitting with. Not the model, the afternoon.

For as long as any of us have been in a classroom, learning anatomy meant looking at a flat page and building the thing in your head. Now you can turn it, open it, and look inside. The imagining step is gone.

And it does not stop at the people who can code. A teacher who picks up these tools can build an interactive application for their own students, for their own subject, without waiting on a publisher or a budget.
